package_info.why_malicious: The package 'event-stream' version 3.3.6 was compromised to include a dependency 'flatmap-stream' containing obfuscated code that harvested Bitcoin wallet credentials from the Copay application and exfiltrated them to a remote server.

execution_context.trigger: During runtime when the Copay application processes wallet data using the flatmap-stream dependency

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code checks if the environment variable 'npm_package_name' is set to 'copay-dash', indicating it is running within the Copay wallet application. If so, it harvests sensitive wallet data and exfiltrates it to a remote server using an HTTP request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code contains obfuscated logic that conditionally executes only when running in a specific application context (Copay), and performs unauthorized data harvesting and exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A typical npm package, especially a stream utility, should not contain obfuscated code, check for specific application names, or access and transmit sensitive wallet data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may use environment variables for configuration, but should not use them to target specific applications for data theft. Data exfiltration is never legitimate in this context.
key_indicators: Use of crypto module and file system access to extract wallet data
HTTP requests to external server for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: Upon installation of event-stream@3.3.6, which pulls in flatmap-stream as a dependency

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The event-stream package was updated to include flatmap-stream as a dependency, which was not present in previous versions. This allowed the malicious code to be included in downstream applications.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The sudden addition of a new, previously unknown dependency (flatmap-stream) to a popular package is a common supply chain attack vector.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package updates should not introduce obscure dependencies without clear justification or transparency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Packages may add dependencies for new features, but such changes are typically documented and reviewed. Here, the addition was stealthy and enabled malicious code execution.
key_indicators: Unexpected addition of flatmap-stream@0.1.1 as a dependency in event-stream@3.3.6
No legitimate code changes in event-stream itself, only dependency update

attack_chain.action: event-stream@3.3.6 is installed, pulling in flatmap-stream@0.1.1 as a dependency
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code from flatmap-stream is included in the application

attack_chain.action: Application (e.g., Copay) executes code from flatmap-stream during normal operation
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code checks for Copay context and harvests wallet data

attack_chain.action: Harvested wallet data is exfiltrated to a remote server controlled by the attacker
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive user wallet credentials

behavioral_signatures: Presence of obfuscated code in node_modules/flatmap-stream/index.js
Unexpected network requests from flatmap-stream to external domains during runtime
Access to wallet data files by flatmap-stream code
network_indicators: Requests to http://psfmalert.com (as identified in the original report)
Any outbound HTTP requests from flatmap-stream code
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan for the presence of flatmap-stream@0.1.1 as a dependency of event-stream@3.3.6. Inspect node_modules/flatmap-stream/index.js for obfuscated code and conditional logic targeting 'copay-dash'. Monitor for unexpected outbound HTTP requests from the flatmap-stream code, especially to http://psfmalert.com. Flag any access to wallet data files by this dependency.
